title: Build SessionRelayManager — autonomous session relay to prevent context rot without requiring a human to paste a handoff into a new session
description:
Design doc: docs/session-relay-design.md (this repo, on main once the docs PR merges).

Problem: anti-compact's PreCompact-hook approach can only ever block/prompt a human to paste
a handoff into a fresh session — it has no channel to inject a new turn autonomously, and it
only ever sees an estimated (chars/4) context usage, never the CLI's exact
get_context_usage percentage. cc-vscode-ext already owns every primitive needed to fix this
properly: it drives claude via --input-format/--output-format stream-json, already polls
exact get_context_usage per channel (MessageBroker.refreshContextUsage), can hold multiple
concurrent session processes (ClaudeProcessManager, one per channelId), and already has
sendUserMessage() to inject a turn into a live process's stdin.

Scope (see the design doc for full detail, file:line citations, and the permission-prompt
race risk to design around):
- src/relay/SessionRelayManager.ts — watches context_usage, triggers a relay at a
  configurable threshold (~65-70%).
- src/relay/handoffPrompt.ts — anti-compact's handoff SYSTEM_PROMPT, copied verbatim,
  injected via the existing sendUserMessage() rather than a second claude -p process.
- ClaudeProcessManager.swapChannel(channelId, options, cwd) — new method: atomically retire
  the old process handle and spawn the new one under the same channelId in one map mutation.
- New IPC types in types/ipc.ts: a relay_started broadcast + a threshold get/set pair.
- Must check ControlRequestManager for a pending control request (e.g. an in-flight
  tool_permission_request, since this repo launches claude with
  --permission-prompt-tool stdio) before swapping, deferring to the next result event
  rather than force-closing mid-prompt.

PROCESS REQUIREMENT: this is real code, not a docs-only change. It must go through Joe's
normal spec -> superpowers:writing-plans -> superpowers:subagent-driven-development pipeline
before any implementation lands — do not implement directly from this ticket or the design
doc alone.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #11 (merged 259c644): SessionRelayManager built via 8-task subagent-driven-development plan, plus 6 review-driven fix rounds (mid-turn relay trigger, close-during-swap, stale-stdout race, live-settings sync, queued-message loss, abort-on-close). 4 follow-up tickets filed: session-relay-design-u8o, session-relay-design-kiw, session-relay-design-x45, session-relay-design-gyf.

title: Relay handoff/reseed turns pollute the transcript UI
description:
SessionRelayManager injects the handoff prompt and the reseed text as real user turns via sendUserMessage(). MessageBroker broadcasts every non-control_response stream event unconditionally, so the assistant's responses to both injected turns render as ordinary, unmarked chat bubbles - the handoff summary (long, meant for the new process, not human eyes) and the reseed ack both appear inline with no visual distinction from real conversation.

A second consequence: the handoff turn's result event flips the channel's `running` state to false in the webview (sessionStore.ts), re-enabling the chat input before the swap/reseed actually finish. A user message typed in that window can land on the dying old process (silently lost) or interleave with the reseed prompt on the new process.

Found during final branch review of feat/session-relay (SessionRelayManager, merged). Explicitly accepted as a non-blocking, tracked follow-up rather than a merge blocker, since docs/session-relay-design.md already named "UI treatment of relay_started" as an out-of-scope non-goal - but the current behavior is actively misleading (unexplained assistant chatter, briefly-reopened input), not just "no UI treatment."

Fix options: suppress the handoff/reseed turns' request broadcasts from the transcript (only broadcast relay_started), or tag them so the webview can filter/collapse them; don't flip running:false until the whole relay completes, not just the handoff sub-turn.
close_reason: Verified resolved by current code: SessionRelayManager.relay() sets relaying.add() synchronously with no leak window (isRelaying() true for entire handoff+swap+reseed span), and MessageBroker.ts:408-427 already gates both the raw stream broadcast and context-usage broadcast on !relaying. webview sessionStore.ts only flips running:false from the suppressed request/result branch, not from context_usage or relay_started. Both halves of the ticket (unmarked chat bubbles + premature running:false) are already covered.

title: Add real end-to-end integration test for the permission-prompt relay defer
description:
docs/session-relay-design.md's own Verification approach section asks for an integration-level test: start a relay-eligible channel, issue a tool call that requires approval, fire a relay trigger mid-prompt, assert the relay defers rather than orphaning the pending tool_permission_request. Task 6 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-session-relay-manager.md covers the equivalent behavior with a fake ControlRequestManager (hasPending() returns true -> relay defers), which is real coverage of the logic, but nothing exercises it against an actual spawned process end-to-end.

Explicitly deferred in the implementation plan pending real usage of the feature to justify the added test infra. Not a merge blocker for feat/session-relay.

title: SessionRelayManager relay() can hang forever with no timeout on capture promises
description:
relay()'s captureNextResult() promises (handoff capture, reseed capture) have no timeout. If the old or new claude process never emits a result event (crash, hang), the promise never resolves/rejects, relaying stays true forever for that channel (blocking all future relay attempts), and there's no visible symptom - the relay feature just silently stops working for that channel until unregisterChannel (channel close) happens to release the stuck flag via the reject path.

Found during code review of SessionRelayManager (Task 6, feat/session-relay branch, merged). Accepted as a known gap, not a merge blocker.

Suggested fix: add a timeout to captureNextResult, and surface some signal (not just silence) when a relay gets stuck - a timeout alone still leaves "the relay silently never happened" as the failure mode.

title: ClaudeProcessManager.swapChannel: partial-launch leak + residual overlapping-swap defects
description:
Found during the final whole-branch review of fix/relay-followup-cleanup (which fixed the two swapChannel edge cases originally tracked as session-relay-design-gyf). Two related, currently-unreachable gaps remain, both because swapChannel() still has exactly one caller (SessionRelayManager), serialized by its own relaying guard, so none of this is reachable yet:

1. Partial-launch leak inside _launchProcess(): _launchProcess() spawns the child process first (spawnFn), then does post-spawn wiring (stdout listener, close/error handlers) that can itself throw (e.g. if proc.stdout is unexpectedly null). If that wiring throws, the already-spawned child process handle is never returned to swapChannel(), so swapChannel()'s failure-path cleanup (added in fix/relay-followup-cleanup) has nothing to kill — the process leaks. Unreachable today because stdio is hardcoded to ['pipe','pipe','pipe']. Cheapest fix: wrap the post-spawn wiring in _launchProcess() in its own try/catch that kills the just-spawned proc and rethrows — this also covers the same gap in spawnClaude(), which shares _launchProcess().

2. Three residual defects in overlapping swapChannel() calls for the same channelId (beyond the reentrancy-token fix already landed):
   a. In an A-fails/B-in-flight overlap, _cleanupIfCurrent() no-ops because B's token still holds the guard, so A's old process gets killed but its stale processes-map entry survives until B resolves.
   b. On a successful overlap, call B snapshots oldProc at its own start (before A's processes.set() ran) — so procA (installed by A, then replaced by B) is never explicitly killed by anyone, only by its own eventual close/error handler.
   c. The failure path's closeRequested.delete(channelId) is unconditional, so it can drop a close request that actually belongs to a different overlapping call (B's), not the one that just failed (A's).

Must be resolved before any second caller of swapChannel() is added, or before SessionRelayManager itself starts retrying/overlapping swaps.

title: ClaudeProcessManager: two narrow swapChannel edge cases (currently unreachable)
description:
Found during code review of swapChannel()'s router-race fix (feat/session-relay branch, merged). Both are narrow, currently-unreachable edge cases since nothing calls swapChannel() except SessionRelayManager, which itself doesn't retry/overlap swaps yet:

1. Compound-failure zombie registration: if the OLD process dies during the swap's await window AND the subsequent _launchProcess call also fails, the old process's close/error is correctly suppressed by the `swapping` guard (no premature unregister), but nothing re-processes it afterward - this.processes still points at the now-dead oldProc, hasChannel() reports true, the router still delivers to it, but writeToChannel silently no-ops forever and no future close/error will fire to trigger cleanup.

2. `swapping` is a per-channelId boolean (a Set), not reentrant-safe: if two swapChannel() calls for the same channelId ever overlap, the first clearing the flag would silently reopen the second's protection window. Not currently reachable (no concurrent-swap caller exists), but worth a counter/per-call-token if a second relay-triggering path is ever added.

Not merge blockers - just worth fixing before anything besides SessionRelayManager's single-caller pattern starts calling swapChannel.
